en.title: Flash-sale booking and inventory: finding and removing the hot-stock bottleneck
en.excerpt: Diagnose why the synchronous Book → Inventory lock → Payment path collapses during double-day promotions, calculate the hot-SKU threshold, and redesign admission, holds and payment for bounded load.
en.scope: The pictured architecture serves one million daily users and roughly ten times normal promotional traffic, but the dangerous number is not daily users or total requests. Product pages multiply reads into inventory checks, while every buyer of one discounted SKU contends on the same stock record or Redis lock. The initial Book → Inventory → Payment chain couples failures: admission arrives too late, a payment command can be lost after a hold commits, and scaling pods cannot raise one hot key's serial capacity. This design makes the bottleneck measurable, gives Inventory one authoritative decision, and operates explicit low-traffic, pre-peak, surge, protection and recovery modes so each component is pre-warmed, autoscaled, capped or scaled in safely.
functional: Serve product/search availability from a versioned projection; revalidate only when creating an authoritative hold.
Admission control: Admit a bounded number of checkout attempts per campaign/SKU and return sold-out, queued or retry-after responses before the inventory authority saturates.
Authoritative hold: Create an idempotent hold with quantity, fencing version and expiry using one atomic conditional write; never keep a database transaction open while calling payment.
Booking saga: Run authorize/capture and order confirmation as a durable saga, release expired or failed holds and reconcile unknown PSP outcomes.
Client-facing state: Expose campaign state, queue position and truthful pending/sold-out results so clients do not poll inventory aggressively.
Durable handoff: Commit stock, expiring hold and outbox together; emit hold-created/payment work only after commit, then return confirm-or-release commands to the Inventory authority.
Traffic lifecycle: Operate NORMAL, PRE_PEAK, SURGE, PROTECT and RECOVERY policies with versioned admission, DB/PSP budgets, user response and rollback owner.

Backpressure contract: Stop or slow producer work before the scarce boundary with bounded admission, in-flight holds, consumer pull/prefetch, deadlines, cancellation, Retry-After and load shedding; never hide overload in an unbounded queue.
quality: Inventory invariant: Confirmed plus active-held quantity never exceeds sellable stock; Redis cache or lock loss cannot violate this invariant.
Overload isolation: Search remains available during checkout overload, and overload for one campaign/SKU cannot consume every DB connection or worker.
Idempotency boundary: The API is idempotent across client retry, gateway retry, queue redelivery and payment callback duplication.
Admission deadline: p99 hold latency stays within the admission deadline; once the queue cannot drain inside the business window, reject rather than hide demand in an unbounded backlog.
Audit trail: Every hold, expiry, payment and compensation transition is auditable and can be replayed or reconciled without mutating history.
Scale-in safety: A worker drains or checkpoints its current message before termination; scale-in cannot strand an active hold, unpublished outbox event or unknown payment.
Budget isolation: Browse, batch and analytics work have bounded DB/PSP concurrency so a scale-out in one path cannot consume the reservation budget.

Backpressure safety: When arrival rate exceeds drain rate, queue age and deadline misses stay bounded by rejecting, shedding or slowing work before DB connections, locks and PSP concurrency are exhausted.
capacity: Baseline: 1M DAU does not imply high throughput—uniform traffic is only 11.6 user arrivals/s. Model the launch window: 50k users refreshing five times in 60 seconds produces about 4,167 edge requests/s before images and retries.

Read amplification: if a page checks 20 SKUs separately, 4,000 page requests/s becomes 80,000 inventory lookups/s. Batch the read, serve a denormalized projection/cache, and remove authoritative inventory from the browse path.

Hot-SKU serialization: capacity is approximately 1 / critical-section time. A 12 ms atomic reservation has a theoretical ceiling near 83 reservations/s for one serialized key; operate around 60–70% (about 50–58/s) to leave failover and variance headroom.

Hot-key slowdown: If lock/transaction time rises to 25 ms under WAL, replication or index pressure, the same SKU falls to 40/s theoretical and roughly 24–28/s safe. Ten application replicas do not raise this per-key limit; they only create more waiters.

Connection bound: 120 usable DB connections with 40 ms average transaction time suggests 3,000 tx/s only when work is independent. One hot row remains limited by its serial service time; if synchronous payment holds each connection for 0.8 s, the same pool has a theoretical ceiling of only 150 checkout/s.

Example admission: benchmark p99 atomic hold at 12 ms, choose 50 hold attempts/s per hot SKU, cap the waiting room at 10 seconds (500 admitted attempts), and reject/mark sold-out beyond it. These are planning numbers, not product guarantees.

Production limit: Find the real knee with a production-shaped pgbench/custom load test: Poisson arrivals plus a flash burst, realistic hot-SKU skew, WAL/replica settings and indexes. Increase target rate until schedule lag, p99 lock wait, serialization retry or error budget rises non-linearly; set the production limit below that point.

Capacity SLOs: DB pool below 70%, p99 lock wait below 20 ms, hold success response below 250 ms, post-admission backend queue age below 2 s, payment pending age bounded by provider SLA, and zero negative inventory.

Autoscaler gap: if a fleet needs 90 seconds to start and safe admission is 50/s while a campaign sends 2,000/s, an unbounded queue grows by roughly 175,500 requests before warm-up completes. Pre-warm known events; use the waiting room to bound unknown spikes.

Scaling vector: CDN, cache, search, gateways and independent workers scale with replicas; a viral SKU remains bounded by its 1 / critical-section rate. Measure and set a separate per-SKU admission cap rather than treating total RPS as capacity.

Scale-in gate: reduce capacity only after no active campaign, queue/outbox age is inside SLO, payment unknown and expiry backlog are draining, and p99/pool/lock signals are stable through a cooldown window.

Backpressure capacity check: admit only when drain_rate exceeds arrival_rate and estimated_drain_time fits the business window; otherwise cap the waiting room, shed low-priority work or return Retry-After instead of growing backlog.
en.diagram_title: Traffic-lifecycle flash-sale architecture with authoritative inventory
data_model: Campaign/SKU policy — campaign_id, sku_id, sellable quota, per-user limit, admission rate, burst, start/end time and policy version.
Inventory position — sku/warehouse partition key, on_hand, reserved, sold, safety stock, monotonic version and last fencing token; enforce reserved + sold ≤ sellable in the authoritative transaction.
Hold — hold_id, sku, user, quantity, state, idempotency key/fingerprint, fencing version and expires_at; one active hold per business key where policy requires it.
Payment/order saga — own payment intent, hold reference, provider attempt, deadline and next action; pending and unknown are explicit states and it never shares an inventory transaction.
Reservation command — command_id, hold_id, sku_id, quantity, idempotency key, admission token and deadline; replay-safe at the booking boundary.
Distributed lock/fencing — lock key, owner, fencing token, lease deadline and authoritative inventory version; stale owners are rejected by the writer.
Inventory update event — event_id, sku_id, inventory_version, delta/state snapshot and occurred_at; partitioned by SKU for ordered projections.
Payment result event — payment_intent_id, order_id, provider_attempt, outcome, idempotency key and received_at; unknown is a first-class outcome.
Outbox/inbox — stable event ID, aggregate/version, payload schema and publish/consume status for idempotent propagation.
Capacity policy — campaign mode, warm-up window, min/max replicas, per-SKU admission rate, DB/PSP budget, cooldown and policy version; every mode change is auditable and reversible.
Worker drain lease — consumer, message/partition, visibility deadline, checkpoint and termination state; prevents scale-in from losing work or duplicating an external effect.
Availability projection — campaign/SKU, approximate remaining band, version and observed_at; optimized for browse and never authoritative for confirmation.
stack: Edge waiting room/CDN — absorbs synchronized refreshes and releases signed admission tokens at a rate the checkout path has measured it can sustain; its bounded queue age is the first backpressure valve; alternative is immediate 429/sold-out for very short campaigns.
API gateway limiter — limits per campaign, SKU, account and device/API key; weighted checkout cost is more useful than IP-only request count behind NAT or bot networks.

PostgreSQL/MySQL inventory authority — conditional UPDATE or short SELECT FOR UPDATE transaction with unique constraints; preferred when oversell is unacceptable because correctness survives cache loss.

Redis — excellent for waiting-room counters, admission tokens, cached availability and optional atomic reservation when bounded loss/repair is explicitly accepted; a TTL lock alone is not the stock source of truth.

Booking lock/fencing — use a short-lived lock or single-writer SKU partition only around the reservation decision; attach a monotonically increasing fencing token so a paused owner cannot write after lease expiry.

Inventory-update MQ — publish the committed stock/hold change through a transactional outbox; partition by SKU, process at least once, dedupe by event ID/version and route poison messages to a visible DLQ.
Payment-result MQ — PSP adapters publish authorized, failed, canceled or unknown results; consumers advance the order state idempotently and reconcile unknown outcomes before release/refund.
Payment guard — use idempotency key + unique payment intent + versioned state transition as the payment lock; never hold the inventory lock or DB transaction while waiting for PSP.
Kafka/RabbitMQ plus transactional outbox — notification, projection and analytics leave the reservation transaction; consumers are idempotent and expose oldest-message age and DLQ ownership.
Durable workflow/orchestrator — owns hold → payment → confirm/release deadlines and status queries; cron-only compensation is simpler but reacts slowly and hides per-order progress.

Scheduled pre-warm — for predictable campaigns, raise the critical path's minimum replicas, cache working set and connection budget before the start time; measure startup/warm-up rather than assuming reactive autoscaling is instant.

Per-component autoscaling — scale UI/API from concurrency or requests/target, queue workers from oldest-message age plus per-partition lag, and payment from pending age; cap each by its DB/PSP downstream budget.

Drain-first scale-in — remove only idle/stateless capacity after queue/outbox/payment/expiry gates are healthy; workers stop pulling, finish or checkpoint, then release their lease before termination.

Cost tiers — analytics, reindex and bulk notifications may scale to zero; checkout API/payment floor, inventory authority, outbox, expiry, callback receiver and HA data stores must retain a minimum safe capacity.
Observability — trace admission-to-hold-to-payment, measure per-SKU lock wait/attempt/success without SKU as an unbounded metric label, and log sampled high-cardinality campaign/SKU details.
tradeoffs: Synchronous boundary should end after the authoritative hold decision: admission, booking and inventory write return held/queued/sold-out. Payment authorization and result delivery cross an asynchronous saga boundary, so the API can return pending without holding a connection.

Booking lock/fencing protects the short concurrent write, but a distributed lock must never span the PSP call. Payment uses an idempotency guard and versioned state machine instead; otherwise a slow PSP turns lock expiry into double-spend or oversell risk.

Inventory-update and payment-result MQs improve isolation but are at-least-once. Ordering is per aggregate/SKU, not global; require event IDs, inbox dedupe, retry with backoff, DLQ ownership and reconciliation dashboards.

Reactive autoscaling saves steady-state cost but acts after measurement, scheduling and warm-up. Scheduled pre-warm costs idle capacity yet is the only reliable response for a campaign whose launch minute is already known.

Scale-out must use a component's own proportional signal: CPU/request concurrency for stateless APIs, oldest event age and partition skew for workers, and DB/PSP budgets as hard caps. A single global CPU target hides the first saturated dependency.

Scale-to-zero is attractive for analytics, reindex and bulk notification, but wrong for the inventory authority, hold expiry, outbox relay, PSP callback and reconciliation paths. Their idle cost buys correctness and a bounded recovery time.

The original shared Book+Payment database minimizes early hops but couples deployments, pools and failures. Separate Inventory/Hold ownership from Payment/Order saga ownership; connect them with outbox events rather than an implicit cross-DB transaction.
A cache or read replica removes browse load, not a hot inventory write. A quota bucket/cell or single-writer lane can isolate a viral SKU, but adds stranded quota, fairness and reconciliation costs.

Synchronous payment gives a final response but holds threads, connections and possibly stock during the slowest dependency. A saga returns pending sooner and adds idempotency, reconciliation and a more complex user contract.

Database conditional updates give the clearest invariant and a per-hot-key serial ceiling. Redis atomic scripts are faster but move durability, failover and repair assumptions into application correctness.
A waiting room protects the system and improves fairness, but exact queue position is expensive and misleading under abandonment; return a band or estimated wait instead.

A longer hold TTL improves checkout completion while reducing inventory utilization and enabling hoarding. Use a short base TTL, per-user caps and policy-controlled extension after payment authorization begins.

Partitioning by SKU spreads different products but never scales one viral SKU. For that key, reduce critical-section time, pre-split a quota into fenced buckets or serialize commands in one partition and accept bounded throughput.

Pre-allocating stock to cells/regions removes a global write hop and contains failure, but stranded quota can show sold-out in one cell while another has stock; rebalance only through fenced quota transfer.

Queueing/backpressure smooths a burst only when drain rate exceeds sustainable arrivals soon enough. If 2,000 attempts/s enter a 50/s hot-SKU worker, backlog grows 1,950/s; after ten seconds it already needs about 390 seconds to drain, so bounded admission and rejection are the honest response.

Failure review: test Redis loss, DB primary failover, an expired hold racing with payment success, duplicated payment callbacks, outbox lag, bot-distributed identities and a client retry storm after a gateway timeout.

code_samples.title: Atomic hot-SKU admission
code_samples.note: Redis performs the cheap admission check atomically; Inventory DB remains the final source of truth.

failure_review.question: What invariant can break, and what keeps it true?
failure_review.answer: The only non-negotiable invariant is confirmed plus active-held quantity never exceeding sellable stock. Inventory DB is the write authority: one conditional reservation write commits position, hold and outbox together; cache, Redis lock and projections are never allowed to confirm stock. If reconciliation detects a mismatch, freeze admission for that SKU and repair from immutable hold, order and PSP evidence rather than editing the stock counter by hand.

failure_review.question: Which signal detects the incident before customers see a collapse?
failure_review.answer: Alert on the first saturated boundary, not aggregate CPU: p99 inventory lock wait above 20 ms, hold latency above 250 ms, usable DB pool above 70%, post-admission queue age above 2 s, hot-partition lag, PSP unknown age and attempt-to-original retry ratio. The campaign dashboard must show these per campaign and sampled hot SKU, with a named owner who can move the mode to PROTECT.

failure_review.question: How is the blast radius contained during a hot SKU or dependency failure?
failure_review.answer: Admission is capped per campaign/SKU before Book and Inventory; checkout has bounded DB and PSP concurrency separate from browse, batch and analytics. In PROTECT, lower the SKU admission rate, stop optional work, serve cached approximate availability and return queued, retry-after or sold-out instead of accumulating an unbounded backend queue. Search stays available because it never calls the authoritative stock write path.

failure_review.question: Can retries duplicate, reorder or incorrectly finalize work?
failure_review.answer: A client idempotency key maps to one hold, payment intent and terminal response; event IDs plus inbox dedupe make MQ redelivery harmless. Ordering is only per SKU/aggregate, so every state transition checks its expected version and a stale confirm/release is rejected. PSP timeout becomes PAYMENT_UNKNOWN: query and reconcile the provider before capture retry, release or refund; never use a Redis lease as proof that a payment may be repeated.

failure_review.question: How do we prove recovery after Redis loss, DB failover or a partial saga?
failure_review.answer: Rebuild projections from the inventory outbox, replay idempotently by aggregate/version, and compare every active hold with payment/order saga and PSP records. The expiry worker reconciles old holds, while a dedicated unknown-payment job queries the PSP and emits one fenced confirm, release or refund decision. Recovery is complete only when the reconciliation diff is zero, queue/outbox and expiry age return inside SLO, and the audit trail can explain each stock transition.

vi.title: Flash-sale booking & inventory: tìm và gỡ hot-inventory bottleneck
vi.excerpt: Phân tích vì sao synchronous Book → lock Inventory → Payment sụp ở peak, tính hot-SKU limit và redesign admission, hold, payment theo bounded load.
vi.scope: Architecture này phục vụ 1M DAU và khoảng 10× traffic trong campaign, nhưng con số nguy hiểm không phải DAU hay total requests. Product page amplify read thành nhiều inventory check, trong khi mọi buyer của một discounted SKU cùng tranh chấp một stock row hoặc Redis lock. Chuỗi ban đầu Book → Inventory → Payment ghép failure lại với nhau: admission đến quá muộn, payment command có thể mất sau khi hold commit và scale pod không thể tăng serial capacity của một hot key. Design này biến bottleneck thành số đo được, giữ Inventory là authoritative decision duy nhất và vận hành explicit mode low-traffic, pre-peak, surge, protect, recovery để mỗi component được pre-warm, autoscale, cap hoặc scale-in an toàn.
functional: Serve availability cho product/search từ projection có version; chỉ revalidate khi tạo hold authoritative.
Kiểm soát admission: Admit số checkout attempt hữu hạn theo campaign/SKU và trả sold-out, queued hoặc retry-after trước khi inventory authority saturation.
Hold authoritative: Tạo hold idempotent có quantity, fencing version và expiry bằng một atomic conditional write; không giữ database transaction khi gọi payment.
Booking saga: Chạy authorize/capture và order confirmation bằng durable saga, release hold hết hạn/thất bại và reconcile PSP outcome mơ hồ.
Trạng thái cho client: Expose campaign state, queue position và pending/sold-out trung thực để client không poll inventory hung hãn.
Handoff bền vững: Commit stock, hold có expiry và outbox cùng nhau; chỉ phát hold-created/payment work sau commit, rồi gửi command confirm/release về Inventory authority.
Traffic lifecycle: Vận hành policy NORMAL, PRE_PEAK, SURGE, PROTECT và RECOVERY có versioned admission, DB/PSP budget, user response và rollback owner.

Backpressure contract: Dừng hoặc làm chậm producer trước scarce boundary bằng bounded admission, in-flight hold, consumer pull/prefetch, deadline, cancellation, Retry-After và load shedding; không giấu overload trong queue vô hạn.
quality: Invariant inventory: Tổng confirmed và active-held không vượt sellable stock; mất Redis cache/lock không được làm vỡ invariant này.
Cô lập quá tải: Search vẫn available khi checkout overload, và overload của một campaign/SKU không ăn hết DB connection hoặc worker.
Ranh giới idempotency: API idempotent qua client retry, gateway retry, queue redelivery và payment callback duplicate.
Hạn admission: p99 hold latency nằm trong admission deadline; khi queue không drain kịp business window phải reject thay vì giấu demand trong backlog vô hạn.
Dấu vết audit: Mọi transition hold, expiry, payment và compensation đều audit/replay/reconcile được mà không mutate history.
Scale-in an toàn: Worker drain hoặc checkpoint message hiện tại trước terminate; scale-in không được làm stranded active hold, outbox chưa publish hoặc payment unknown.
Cô lập budget: Browse, batch và analytics có DB/PSP concurrency hữu hạn để scale-out một path không ăn reservation budget.
Backpressure safety: Khi arrival rate vượt drain rate, queue age và deadline miss vẫn hữu hạn bằng cách reject, shed hoặc làm chậm work trước khi DB connection, lock và PSP concurrency cạn.
capacity: Baseline: 1M DAU không đồng nghĩa throughput cao — nếu đều chỉ là 11,6 user arrival/s. Cần model launch window: 50k user refresh năm lần trong 60 giây tạo khoảng 4.167 edge request/s, chưa tính image và retry.

Read amplification: nếu mỗi page check riêng 20 SKU, 4.000 page request/s biến thành 80.000 inventory lookup/s. Phải batch read, serve projection/cache denormalized và bỏ inventory authoritative khỏi browse path.

Hot-SKU serialization: capacity xấp xỉ 1 / thời gian critical section. Atomic reservation 12 ms có trần lý thuyết gần 83 reservation/s cho một key serialized; chỉ vận hành 60–70% (khoảng 50–58/s) để chừa headroom cho variance/failover.

Chậm ở hot key: Nếu lock/transaction tăng lên 25 ms do WAL, replication hoặc index pressure, cùng SKU chỉ còn 40/s lý thuyết và khoảng 24–28/s an toàn. Mười app replica không tăng per-key limit; chúng chỉ tạo thêm waiter.

Connection bound: 120 DB connection dùng được với average transaction time 40 ms gợi ý 3.000 tx/s chỉ khi work độc lập. Một hot row vẫn bị giới hạn bởi serial service time; nếu synchronous payment giữ mỗi connection 0,8 giây thì cùng pool chỉ còn trần lý thuyết 150 checkout/s.

Ví dụ admission: benchmark p99 atomic hold 12 ms, chọn 50 hold attempt/s cho mỗi hot SKU, cap waiting room 10 giây (500 attempt đã admit), reject/mark sold-out phần vượt. Đây là planning number, không phải guarantee chung.

Giới hạn production: Tìm knee thật bằng pgbench/custom load test giống production: Poisson arrival cộng flash burst, hot-SKU skew thật, WAL/replica/index thật. Tăng target rate tới khi schedule lag, p99 lock wait, serialization retry hoặc error budget tăng phi tuyến; đặt production limit thấp hơn điểm đó.
Capacity SLO: DB pool dưới 70%, p99 lock wait dưới 20 ms, hold response dưới 250 ms, post-admission backend queue age dưới 2 giây, payment pending age theo provider SLA và zero negative inventory.

Khoảng trống autoscaler: Nếu fleet cần 90 giây để start và safe admission là 50/s trong khi campaign gửi 2.000/s, queue vô hạn tăng khoảng 175.500 request trước khi warm-up xong. Campaign có lịch phải pre-warm; spike không biết trước phải bị waiting room chặn hữu hạn.

Scaling vector: CDN, cache, search, gateway và worker độc lập scale theo replica; một SKU viral vẫn bị chặn bởi 1 / critical-section time. Đo và đặt per-SKU admission cap riêng thay vì xem total RPS là capacity.
Gate scale-in: Chỉ giảm capacity khi không có active campaign, queue/outbox age trong SLO, payment unknown và expiry backlog đang drain, p99/pool/lock ổn định qua cooldown window.

Backpressure capacity check: Chỉ admit khi drain_rate lớn hơn arrival_rate và estimated_drain_time nằm trong business window; nếu không thì cap waiting room, shed work ít ưu tiên hoặc trả Retry-After thay vì để backlog phình.

data_model: Campaign/SKU policy — campaign_id, sku_id, sellable quota, per-user limit, admission rate/burst, start/end và policy version.
Inventory position — partition key sku/warehouse, on_hand, reserved, sold, safety stock, monotonic version và last fencing token; enforce reserved + sold ≤ sellable trong transaction authoritative.
Hold — hold_id, sku, user, quantity, state, idempotency key/fingerprint, fencing version và expires_at; một active hold trên mỗi business key khi policy yêu cầu.
Payment/order saga — sở hữu payment intent, hold reference, provider attempt, deadline và next action; pending/unknown là state rõ ràng và không share inventory transaction.
Reservation command — command_id, hold_id, sku_id, quantity, idempotency key, admission token và deadline; replay-safe ở booking boundary.
Distributed lock/fencing — lock key, owner, fencing token, lease deadline và inventory version authoritative; writer từ owner cũ sẽ bị reject.
Inventory update event — event_id, sku_id, inventory_version, delta/state snapshot và occurred_at; partition theo SKU để projection có thứ tự.
Payment result event — payment_intent_id, order_id, provider_attempt, outcome, idempotency key và received_at; unknown là outcome chính thức.
Outbox/inbox — stable event ID, aggregate/version, payload schema và publish/consume status cho propagation idempotent.
Capacity policy — campaign mode, warm-up window, min/max replica, per-SKU admission rate, DB/PSP budget, cooldown và policy version; mọi mode change audit/rollback được.
Worker drain lease — consumer, message/partition, visibility deadline, checkpoint và termination state; ngăn scale-in làm mất work hoặc duplicate external effect.
Availability projection — campaign/SKU, approximate remaining band, version và observed_at; tối ưu browse và không authoritative khi confirm.
stack: Edge waiting room/CDN — hấp thụ synchronized refresh và phát signed admission token theo rate checkout path đã đo là chịu được; bounded queue age là van backpressure đầu tiên; campaign rất ngắn có thể chọn 429/sold-out ngay.
API gateway limiter — limit theo campaign, SKU, account và device/API key; weighted checkout cost hữu ích hơn IP-only count sau NAT hoặc bot network.
PostgreSQL/MySQL inventory authority — conditional UPDATE hoặc transaction SELECT FOR UPDATE rất ngắn kèm unique constraint; phù hợp khi không chấp nhận oversell vì correctness sống qua cache loss.

Redis — phù hợp cho waiting-room counter, admission token, cached availability và optional atomic reservation nếu bounded loss/repair được chấp nhận rõ; TTL lock đơn lẻ không phải stock source of truth.
Booking lock/fencing — dùng lock ngắn hoặc single-writer SKU partition chỉ quanh quyết định reservation; gắn fencing token tăng dần để owner bị pause không thể ghi sau khi lease hết hạn.
Inventory-update MQ — publish stock/hold change đã commit qua transactional outbox; partition theo SKU, xử lý at-least-once, dedupe theo event ID/version và đưa poison message vào DLQ nhìn thấy được.
Payment-result MQ — PSP adapter publish authorized, failed, canceled hoặc unknown; consumer tiến state order idempotent và reconcile unknown trước khi release/refund.
Payment guard — dùng idempotency key + unique payment intent + versioned state transition làm payment lock; không giữ inventory lock hay DB transaction khi chờ PSP.
Kafka/RabbitMQ + transactional outbox — đưa notification, projection và analytics ra khỏi reservation transaction; consumer idempotent, quan sát oldest-message age và có DLQ owner.
Durable workflow/orchestrator — sở hữu deadline hold → payment → confirm/release và status query; cron-only compensation đơn giản hơn nhưng phản ứng chậm, giấu progress từng order.
Scheduled pre-warm — campaign có lịch phải nâng min replica critical path, cache working set và connection budget trước giờ mở; đo startup/warm-up thay vì tin reactive autoscale là tức thì.

Autoscaling theo component — UI/API scale từ concurrency hoặc requests/target, queue worker từ oldest-message age cộng per-partition lag, payment từ pending age; mỗi path bị cap bởi DB/PSP downstream budget.
Drain-first scale-in — chỉ bỏ capacity idle/stateless khi gate queue/outbox/payment/expiry khỏe; worker stop pulling, finish/checkpoint rồi release lease trước terminate.

Cost tier — analytics, reindex, bulk notification có thể scale-to-zero; checkout API/payment floor, inventory authority, outbox, expiry, callback receiver và HA datastore phải giữ minimum safe capacity.
Observability — trace admission-to-hold-to-payment, đo lock wait/attempt/success theo SKU mà không dùng SKU làm metric label vô hạn, log high-cardinality campaign/SKU theo sampling.
tradeoffs: Ranh giới synchronous nên kết thúc sau authoritative hold: admission, booking và inventory write trả held/queued/sold-out. Payment authorization và result đi qua async saga, API trả pending mà không giữ connection.

Booking lock/fencing bảo vệ concurrent write ngắn, nhưng distributed lock tuyệt đối không được kéo qua PSP. Payment dùng idempotency guard và state machine có version; nếu không PSP chậm sẽ biến lock expiry thành rủi ro double-spend/oversell.

Hai MQ inventory-update và payment-result tăng isolation nhưng là at-least-once. Ordering chỉ bảo đảm theo aggregate/SKU, không global; cần event ID, inbox dedupe, retry backoff, DLQ owner và dashboard reconciliation.

Reactive autoscaling tiết kiệm steady-state cost nhưng chỉ hành động sau measurement, scheduling và warm-up. Scheduled pre-warm tốn idle capacity nhưng là phản ứng đáng tin duy nhất khi đã biết launch minute của campaign.

Scale-out phải dùng proportional signal riêng từng component: CPU/request concurrency cho API stateless, oldest event age và partition skew cho worker, DB/PSP budget là hard cap. Một global CPU target che dependency saturated đầu tiên.

Scale-to-zero hấp dẫn cho analytics, reindex và bulk notification nhưng sai với inventory authority, hold expiry, outbox relay, PSP callback và reconciliation. Idle cost của chúng mua correctness và bounded recovery time.

Shared Book+Payment database ban đầu giảm hop nhưng ghép deployment, pool và failure. Tách ownership Inventory/Hold khỏi Payment/Order saga; nối bằng outbox event thay vì implicit cross-DB transaction.
Cache hoặc read replica gỡ browse load, không gỡ hot inventory write. Quota bucket/cell hoặc single-writer lane có thể isolate viral SKU nhưng thêm stranded quota, fairness và reconciliation cost.

Synchronous payment trả final response nhưng giữ thread, connection và có thể cả stock qua dependency chậm nhất. Saga trả pending sớm hơn nhưng thêm idempotency, reconciliation và user contract phức tạp.
Database conditional update cho invariant rõ nhất và có serial ceiling theo hot key. Redis atomic script nhanh hơn nhưng đưa assumption durability, failover và repair vào correctness của application.
Waiting room bảo vệ hệ thống và tăng fairness, nhưng exact queue position đắt và gây hiểu nhầm khi user abandon; nên trả range hoặc estimated wait.
Hold TTL dài tăng checkout completion nhưng giảm inventory utilization và tạo cơ hội hoarding. Dùng base TTL ngắn, per-user cap và chỉ extend theo policy sau khi bắt đầu payment authorization.

Partition theo SKU phân tán các product khác nhau nhưng không scale một viral SKU. Với key đó phải giảm critical-section time, pre-split quota thành fenced bucket hoặc serialize command trong một partition và chấp nhận bounded throughput.

Pre-allocate stock theo cell/region bỏ global write hop và giới hạn blast radius, nhưng quota có thể mắc kẹt khiến một cell báo sold-out trong khi cell khác còn hàng; chỉ rebalance qua fenced quota transfer.

Queue/backpressure chỉ làm phẳng burst nếu drain rate sớm vượt sustainable arrival. Nếu 2.000 attempt/s vào worker hot-SKU 50/s, backlog tăng 1.950/s; sau 10 giây đã cần khoảng 390 giây để drain, vì vậy bounded admission và reject mới là phản hồi trung thực.

Failure review: test Redis loss, DB primary failover, expired hold race với payment success, duplicate payment callback, outbox lag, bot dùng distributed identity và client retry storm sau gateway timeout.

failure_review.question: Invariant nào có thể vỡ và điều gì giữ nó đúng?
failure_review.answer: Invariant không được phá là confirmed cộng active-held không bao giờ vượt sellable stock. Inventory DB là write authority: một conditional reservation write commit position, hold và outbox cùng transaction; cache, Redis lock hay projection không bao giờ được confirm stock. Nếu reconciliation thấy lệch, freeze admission của SKU đó và repair bằng bằng chứng immutable từ hold, order và PSP, không sửa tay stock counter.

failure_review.question: Tín hiệu nào phát hiện incident trước khi khách thấy hệ thống sụp?
failure_review.answer: Alert ở boundary saturated đầu tiên, không nhìn CPU tổng: p99 inventory lock wait trên 20 ms, hold latency trên 250 ms, usable DB pool trên 70%, post-admission queue age trên 2 giây, hot-partition lag, PSP unknown age và tỉ lệ retry/original attempt. Campaign dashboard phải hiển thị theo campaign và hot SKU được sample, kèm owner có quyền chuyển mode sang PROTECT.

failure_review.question: Blast radius được contain thế nào khi hot SKU hoặc dependency lỗi?
failure_review.answer: Admission bị cap theo campaign/SKU trước Book và Inventory; checkout có DB/PSP concurrency hữu hạn, tách khỏi browse, batch và analytics. Ở PROTECT, giảm SKU admission rate, dừng optional work, serve cached approximate availability và trả queued, retry-after hoặc sold-out thay vì tích backend queue vô hạn. Search vẫn available vì không gọi authoritative stock write path.

failure_review.question: Retry có thể duplicate, reorder hoặc finalize sai không?
failure_review.answer: Client idempotency key map vào một hold, payment intent và terminal response; event ID cộng inbox dedupe làm MQ redelivery vô hại. Ordering chỉ theo SKU/aggregate nên mọi state transition kiểm expected version và stale confirm/release bị reject. PSP timeout thành PAYMENT_UNKNOWN: query và reconcile provider trước khi capture retry, release hoặc refund; không dùng Redis lease làm bằng chứng payment được phép lặp.

failure_review.question: Làm sao chứng minh recovery sau Redis loss, DB failover hoặc saga dang dở?
failure_review.answer: Rebuild projection từ inventory outbox, replay idempotent theo aggregate/version, rồi đối chiếu từng active hold với payment/order saga và PSP record. Expiry worker reconcile hold cũ; unknown-payment job query PSP và phát đúng một fenced decision confirm, release hoặc refund. Recovery chỉ hoàn tất khi reconciliation diff bằng 0, queue/outbox/expiry age về lại SLO và audit trail giải thích được từng stock transition.

en.title: API gateway and identity edge under four traffic tiers
en.excerpt: Choose the edge controls, identity trust boundaries and sync/async hops that keep a gateway useful without turning it into a global bottleneck or a new single point of failure.
en.scope:
Every request needs a defensible authentication and authorization boundary before it reaches the system, but putting every control at one gateway creates a new choke point. The design must separate north-south routing from east-west calls, keep domain authorization with the resource owner, and size identity, rate limiting and connection state against a declared peak workload. It must also say what remains available when the IdP, JWKS, policy engine, Redis or one gateway cell is unhealthy.

The thesis is simple: the edge should make cheap, coarse decisions early, while services retain the authority to protect their own invariants.
functional: Routing: match host, path and method, then apply ordered filters without allowing client headers to change the destination.
Authentication: verify the bearer token or a narrowly scoped internal assertion before protected north-south traffic reaches a service.
Authorization: enforce coarse scope, audience, tenant and product policy at the edge, then leave object and state authorization to the owner service.
Admission: apply per-route, tenant and identity rate limits plus bounded concurrency before scarce downstream capacity is consumed.
Resilience: enforce deadlines, retry budgets, circuit breaking and an explicit 429, 503 or 504 contract for each route.
Identity propagation: forward a verified original token or a signed internal assertion while stripping client-supplied identity headers.
Operations: emit route-level RED metrics, W3C traces, a bounded correlation id and audit-safe policy decisions for diagnosis and review.
quality: Latency budget: target no more than 5 ms p99 for a warm local route, then measure JWT, Redis and PDP costs separately; this is an SLO target, not a vendor guarantee.
Availability: the edge is not a single point of failure; gateway capacity, configuration, keys and policy must survive one instance, zone or cell loss.
Identity outage: cached JWKS may verify an unexpired JWT, but money movement and privilege changes fail closed when the IdP, introspection or policy source is unavailable.
Isolation: one route, tenant, backend, IdP or PDP failure cannot exhaust the connection pool, event loop, limiter state or retry budget of unrelated routes.
Trust boundary: client-provided user, tenant, role, forwarding and routing headers are stripped and rebuilt only from verified context.
Rotation: issuer, key, policy and route changes have overlap, versioning, canary and rollback paths that do not depend on the failing control plane.
Degraded contract: every route declares whether it rejects, serves a bounded stale result, becomes read-only or returns pending when a dependency is unhealthy.
capacity: T1 — 2.5 rps peak (10k req/day): one or two gateway instances, a local or managed limiter and one regional identity path are usually sufficient; measure the added hop rather than guessing.
T2 — 25 rps peak (100k req/day): keep a small multi-instance fleet, warm connection pools and route-level budgets; a shared Redis limiter is useful when tenant or abuse isolation needs it.
T3 — 250 rps peak (1M req/day): size gateway replicas by p99 concurrency and downstream budgets, then add zonal HA, Redis HA, JWKS cache protection, retry budgets and dependency-specific breakers.
Waypoint — 2,500 rps peak (10M req/day): test whether one regional fleet can still upgrade, warm and recover as a unit; this is often where cells or regional policy distribution become worthwhile.

T4 — 25,000 rps peak (100M req/day): model roughly ten T3-to-waypoint cells plus routing, with per-cell gateway instances, local key/cache paths and regional isolation; the fleet-wide number is not a single process target.

JWT and JWKS: benchmark RS256 and ES256 verification at the target p99 with warm and cold key caches, token sizes and realistic concurrency; record cache-hit rate and unknown-kid refresh rate instead of inventing a constant.

Rate limiting: count one Redis atomic check, its retries and policy refresh operations per request, then reserve headroom for hot tenants and failover; measure Redis ops and latency under the actual key distribution.

Boundary trigger: move tier when connection acquisition, event-loop delay, 429/504 rate, retry amplification, JWKS/PDP latency or blast radius breaches the budget even if average CPU is below a target.
en.diagram_title: North-south edge, identity controls and east-west paths
data_model: Route configuration — route id, match predicates, destination, ordered filters, timeout, retry budget, auth mode, policy version and rollback owner; publish it as a validated immutable snapshot.
Rate-limit counter — Redis key, policy version, refill rate, burst, weighted cost, expiry and decision timestamp; counters are disposable control state, not business truth.
JWKS and token cache — issuer, key id, public key, algorithm, fetched_at, expires_at and refresh status; cache public verification material and never private keys or bearer tokens.
Policy and rule store — tenant, principal, action, resource class, policy version, bundle checksum and activation window; a PDP decision is reproducible only when its input and version are known.
Identity assertion — subject, tenant, audience, scopes, issue time, expiry, key id and route context; services verify the assertion before using it and reject a client-created equivalent.
Audit log — decision id, principal pseudonym, tenant, action, route, policy/key version, outcome, reason code and trace id; exclude tokens, secrets and unnecessary payload data.
Capacity and health budget — route, cell, instance, connection limits, queue age, dependency state, warm-up phase and last-known-good config; it drives admission and safe scale-in.
stack: CDN and L4 boundary: terminate or pass through transport concerns, cache safe public bytes and shed obvious abuse before the application gateway; do not put object authorization here.

Spring Cloud Gateway 5.0.2: use the selected Server WebFlux or Server Web MVC starter from the 2025.1.2 release train, and keep route predicates, ordered filters and effective configuration under test.
Runtime baseline: use a supported Java LTS and verify vendor patch support against the selected Boot/Cloud train; JDK 25 is the current LTS reference at review time, not a throughput assumption.

Resilience4j 2.4.0: use CircuitBreaker, TimeLimiter and RateLimiter concepts for local protection, but choose one retry/breaker owner per hop and avoid hiding distributed state behind an in-process default. 2.4.0 is the release that adds Spring Boot 4 support via the separate resilience4j-spring-boot4 starter.

Redis rate limiter and cache: use atomic token-bucket checks, short-lived policy/JWKS metadata and bounded decision cache; isolate limiter state by region or cell when a global store becomes a failure amplifier.

Identity provider and keys: use OAuth/OIDC discovery, short-lived access tokens, overlapping signing keys and regional JWKS availability; validate issuer, audience, algorithm and time at the consumer boundary.
PDP: use OPA/Rego, Cedar or a service-local policy module only for decisions that need dynamic context; version bundles, cache with a stated staleness bound and keep the service invariant local.

Internal protocols: keep public REST at the north-south contract, use gRPC when a measured east-west need justifies it, and use a durable message broker for work that does not belong on the request path.
tradeoffs: Gateway verification vs service verification — verify at both boundaries for defense in depth, but give the gateway coarse rejection and the service final resource authorization; measure the duplicated crypto cost.

JWT vs opaque introspection — JWT keeps the hot path local and survives a bounded IdP outage, while opaque tokens give fresher revocation at the price of an IdP dependency and a cache-staleness contract.
Roles in token vs PDP — token roles are cheap and portable but stale; a PDP handles dynamic resource context but needs availability, policy rollout, decision caching and audit ownership.

Sync vs async hop — synchronous calls preserve an immediate answer but multiply tail latency and retry work; queues smooth load and isolate failure but owe idempotency, ordering, DLQ, lag and a pending contract.

Smart gateway vs thin gateway — domain-aware routing can reduce client hops, but fetching business data at the edge duplicates service ownership, increases blast radius and makes policy evolution harder.

Global state vs cells — one limiter, IdP cache or PDP is simple to reason about initially, while regional or per-cell state limits blast radius but adds quota transfer, key distribution and reconciliation work.

Central config vs local autonomy — a central snapshot gives consistent policy and rollback, while local cached data keeps the data plane alive during control-plane failure; both require version, expiry and last-known-good behavior.

failure_review.question: Which invariant can break when the gateway or IdP is unhealthy?
failure_review.answer: A valid identity must never become a valid domain action by itself. The service remains the authority for tenant, object and state invariants; gateway and IdP failures may reject or degrade a request, but they cannot authorize a client-supplied header or bypass the service check.

failure_review.question: Which metric detects the edge boundary before users see an outage?
failure_review.answer: Start with route-level p99, pending connection acquisition, event-loop delay, 429/504 rate, retry amplification, JWKS/PDP latency and usable downstream pool. The first saturated dependency—not aggregate gateway CPU—sets the next action and the blast radius.

failure_review.question: How is the blast radius contained when one route, cell or identity dependency fails?
failure_review.answer: Scope breakers, limits, pools, caches and policy bundles by route, tenant, region or cell. Fail closed for high-risk actions, serve only explicitly bounded stale reads, and keep last-known-good route and key material so one control-plane failure cannot erase every data-plane decision.

failure_review.question: Can retry duplicate or reorder an external effect?
failure_review.answer: Yes: a gateway timeout does not prove that the service or provider did nothing. Retry only safe operations or carry an idempotency key, keep one retry owner per hop, and use an explicit pending/unknown state with reconciliation for payment or other irreversible effects.

failure_review.question: What evidence proves recovery after key, Redis, PDP or gateway-cell loss?
failure_review.answer: Restore the last-known-good configuration, refresh keys with overlap, rebuild disposable counters and replay policy safely, then verify route error budget, queue age, key refresh, decision consistency and reconciliation debt. Recovery is proven only when the degraded contract ends without an unexplained authorization or business-state transition.

vi.title: API gateway và identity edge dưới bốn traffic tier
vi.excerpt: Chọn edge control, identity trust boundary và sync/async hop để gateway hữu ích mà không thành bottleneck toàn cục hay single point of failure mới.
vi.scope:
Mọi request cần một authentication và authorization boundary có thể bảo vệ được trước khi vào hệ thống, nhưng gom mọi control vào một gateway sẽ tạo choke point mới. Design phải tách north-south routing khỏi east-west call, giữ domain authorization với resource owner, và size identity, rate limiting cùng connection state theo peak workload đã khai báo. Design cũng phải nói rõ còn phục vụ được gì khi IdP, JWKS, policy engine, Redis hoặc một gateway cell không khỏe.

Thesis là: edge nên đưa ra quyết định coarse, rẻ và sớm, còn service giữ authority để bảo vệ invariant của chính nó.
functional: Routing: match host, path và method rồi chạy filter theo thứ tự, không cho client header đổi destination.
Authentication: verify bearer token hoặc internal assertion scope hẹp trước khi north-south traffic được bảo vệ tới service.
Authorization: enforce scope, audience, tenant và product policy ở mức coarse tại edge, rồi để owner service quyết object và state authorization.
Admission: áp dụng rate limit theo route, tenant và identity cùng bounded concurrency trước khi tiêu downstream capacity khan hiếm.
Resilience: enforce deadline, retry budget, circuit breaker và contract rõ cho 429, 503 hoặc 504 của từng route.
Identity propagation: forward original token đã verify hoặc signed assertion, đồng thời strip identity header do client gửi.
Operations: emit RED metrics theo route, W3C trace, correlation id có giới hạn và policy decision an toàn cho audit.
quality: Latency budget: target không quá 5 ms p99 cho route local đã warm, sau đó đo riêng cost của JWT, Redis và PDP; đây là SLO target, không phải vendor guarantee.
Availability: edge không được là single point of failure; gateway capacity, config, key và policy phải sống qua mất instance, zone hoặc cell.
Identity outage: cached JWKS có thể verify JWT chưa hết hạn, nhưng money movement và privilege change phải fail closed khi IdP, introspection hoặc policy source unavailable.
Isolation: route, tenant, backend, IdP hoặc PDP hỏng không được ăn hết connection pool, event loop, limiter state hay retry budget của route khác.
Trust boundary: user, tenant, role, forwarding và routing header từ client phải bị strip rồi dựng lại từ context đã verify.
Rotation: thay issuer, key, policy và route phải có overlap, version, canary và rollback không phụ thuộc control plane đang lỗi.
Degraded contract: từng route phải nói rõ lúc dependency lỗi thì reject, serve stale có giới hạn, chuyển read-only hay trả pending.
capacity: T1 — 2,5 rps peak (10k req/day): một hoặc hai gateway instance, limiter local/managed và một identity path trong region thường đủ; đo hop thêm thay vì đoán.
T2 — 25 rps peak (100k req/day): giữ fleet nhỏ nhiều instance, warm connection pool và budget theo route; shared Redis limiter hữu ích khi cần isolate tenant hoặc abuse.
T3 — 250 rps peak (1M req/day): size gateway replica theo p99 concurrency và downstream budget, rồi thêm zonal HA, Redis HA, JWKS-cache protection, retry budget và breaker theo dependency.
Waypoint — 2.500 rps peak (10M req/day): test một regional fleet còn upgrade, warm và recovery như một unit được không; đây thường là lúc cell hoặc regional policy distribution đáng có.

T4 — 25.000 rps peak (100M req/day): model khoảng mười cell T3 tới waypoint cộng routing, với gateway instance, key/cache path và regional isolation theo cell; không xem số toàn fleet là target của một process.
JWT và JWKS: benchmark verify RS256/ES256 ở p99 mục tiêu với key cache warm/cold, token size và concurrency thật; ghi cache-hit rate cùng unknown-kid refresh rate thay vì bịa constant.
Rate limit: đếm một Redis atomic check, retry và policy refresh cho mỗi request, rồi chừa headroom cho hot tenant và failover; đo Redis ops cùng latency theo key distribution thật.
Boundary trigger: đổi tier khi connection acquisition, event-loop delay, 429/504, retry amplification, JWKS/PDP latency hoặc blast radius vượt budget dù CPU trung bình còn thấp.

data_model: Route configuration — route id, match predicate, destination, ordered filter, timeout, retry budget, auth mode, policy version và rollback owner; publish thành immutable snapshot đã validate.
Rate-limit counter — Redis key, policy version, refill rate, burst, weighted cost, expiry và decision timestamp; đây là control state có thể bỏ, không phải business truth.
JWKS và token cache — issuer, key id, public key, algorithm, fetched_at, expires_at và refresh status; chỉ cache public verification material, không cache private key hay bearer token.
Policy và rule store — tenant, principal, action, resource class, policy version, bundle checksum và activation window; PDP decision chỉ reproduce được khi biết input và version.
Identity assertion — subject, tenant, audience, scope, issue time, expiry, key id và route context; service phải verify assertion rồi mới dùng, không chấp nhận bản client tự tạo.
Audit log — decision id, principal pseudonym, tenant, action, route, policy/key version, outcome, reason code và trace id; không ghi token, secret hay payload thừa.
Capacity và health budget — route, cell, instance, connection limit, queue age, dependency state, warm-up phase và last-known-good config; nó điều khiển admission và scale-in an toàn.
stack: CDN và L4 boundary: xử lý transport, cache public byte an toàn và shed abuse rõ ràng trước application gateway; không đặt object authorization ở đây.
Spring Cloud Gateway 5.0.2: dùng starter Server WebFlux hoặc Server Web MVC đã chọn trong release train 2025.1.2, đưa route predicate, ordered filter và effective config vào test.
Runtime baseline: dùng Java LTS còn được vendor hỗ trợ và verify patch support theo Boot/Cloud train đã chọn; ở thời điểm review, JDK 25 là mốc LTS hiện hành, không phải throughput assumption.

Resilience4j 2.4.0: dùng khái niệm CircuitBreaker, TimeLimiter và RateLimiter cho protection local, nhưng mỗi hop phải có một retry/breaker owner và không giấu distributed state sau default in-process. 2.4.0 là bản thêm hỗ trợ Spring Boot 4 qua starter riêng resilience4j-spring-boot4.
Redis rate limiter và cache: dùng token-bucket check atomic, policy/JWKS metadata ngắn hạn và decision cache có giới hạn; isolate limiter state theo region/cell khi global store khuếch đại failure.
Identity provider và key: dùng OAuth/OIDC discovery, access token ngắn hạn, signing key overlap và JWKS theo region; consumer phải validate issuer, audience, algorithm và time.
PDP: dùng OPA/Rego, Cedar hoặc policy module local khi decision cần context động; version bundle, cache với staleness bound rõ và giữ invariant trong service.
Internal protocol: giữ public REST ở north-south contract, dùng gRPC khi east-west need đã đo đủ để biện minh, và dùng message broker cho work không thuộc request path.
tradeoffs: Gateway verification vs service verification — verify ở cả hai boundary để defense in depth, nhưng gateway reject coarse còn service authorize resource cuối; phải đo crypto cost bị lặp.
JWT vs opaque introspection — JWT giữ hot path local và sống qua IdP outage có giới hạn; opaque token revocation mới hơn nhưng phải trả IdP dependency và cache-staleness contract.
Role trong token vs PDP — token role rẻ, portable nhưng stale; PDP xử lý resource context động nhưng cần availability, policy rollout, decision cache và audit owner.
Sync vs async hop — sync giữ answer ngay nhưng nhân tail latency và retry work; queue làm phẳng load, isolate failure nhưng phải trả idempotency, ordering, DLQ, lag và pending contract.
Smart gateway vs thin gateway — route hiểu domain có thể giảm hop của client, nhưng fetch business data ở edge lặp service ownership, tăng blast radius và làm policy khó evolve.
Global state vs cell — limiter, IdP cache hoặc PDP global ban đầu dễ hiểu hơn; state theo region/cell giảm blast radius nhưng thêm quota transfer, key distribution và reconciliation.
Central config vs local autonomy — snapshot central cho policy nhất quán và rollback, cache local giữ data plane sống khi control plane lỗi; cả hai đều cần version, expiry và last-known-good.

failure_review.question: Invariant nào có thể break khi gateway hoặc IdP không khỏe?
failure_review.answer: Identity hợp lệ không tự biến thành domain action hợp lệ. Service vẫn là authority cho tenant, object và state invariant; gateway/IdP failure có thể reject hoặc degrade nhưng không được authorize client header hay bypass service check.

failure_review.question: Metric nào phát hiện edge boundary trước khi user thấy outage?
failure_review.answer: Bắt đầu với p99 theo route, pending connection acquisition, event-loop delay, 429/504, retry amplification, JWKS/PDP latency và usable downstream pool. Dependency saturation đầu tiên, không phải aggregate CPU, quyết định action kế tiếp và blast radius.

failure_review.question: Blast radius được contain thế nào khi một route, cell hoặc identity dependency lỗi?
failure_review.answer: Scope breaker, limit, pool, cache và policy bundle theo route, tenant, region hoặc cell. Fail closed cho action rủi ro cao, chỉ serve stale khi có bound rõ, và giữ last-known-good route/key để một control-plane failure không xóa mọi data-plane decision.

failure_review.question: Retry có duplicate hoặc reorder external effect không?
failure_review.answer: Có: gateway timeout không chứng minh service/provider chưa làm gì. Chỉ retry operation an toàn hoặc mang idempotency key, giữ một retry owner cho mỗi hop, và dùng pending/unknown state cùng reconciliation cho payment hay external effect không đảo ngược.

failure_review.question: Bằng chứng nào chứng minh recovery sau mất key, Redis, PDP hoặc gateway cell?
failure_review.answer: Restore last-known-good config, refresh key có overlap, rebuild counter có thể bỏ và replay policy an toàn, rồi verify error budget, queue age, key refresh, decision consistency cùng reconciliation debt. Recovery chỉ được coi là xong khi degraded contract kết thúc mà không có authorization hay business transition không giải thích được.

en.title: Fair multi-tenant work scheduling with RabbitMQ
en.excerpt: Prevent one tenant's thousand jobs from hiding another tenant's single job by separating admission, scheduling and execution fairness instead of asking prefetch to solve all three.
en.scope:
Users submit URLs into a multi-stage worker pipeline. Tenant A can enqueue 1,000 jobs while tenant B submits one latency-sensitive job. The goal is bounded wait and predictable resource share without creating one queue and consumer per tenant. RabbitMQ remains the durable delivery layer; a cost-aware scheduler owns fairness.

The key distinction is that routing is not scheduling: hashing tenants, raising prefetch or assigning message priority can improve distribution or throughput, but none alone guarantees that a noisy tenant cannot monopolize downstream capacity.
functional: Accept a job with a tenant id, idempotency key, service class, estimated cost and deadline; return accepted, deferred or rejected explicitly.
Apply per-tenant rate, pending-work and concurrent-cost limits before publishing runnable work.
Schedule active tenants with Deficit Round Robin, allowing tier weights while guaranteeing progress for every tenant inside its contract.
Route admitted jobs to a bounded number of interactive and bulk queues, then preserve tenant context through every processing stage.
Retry transient failures with a separate budget and quarantine poison jobs without resetting their tenant cost.
Expose job state and cancellation without using RabbitMQ queue position as the product source of truth.
quality: Fairness: a sustained bulk producer cannot make another admitted tenant wait indefinitely; define maximum runnable age per service tier.
Backpressure: per-tenant and global backlog are bounded in jobs and estimated cost; overload returns 429 or a truthful deferred state before broker memory becomes the limit.
Isolation: one tenant's retries, slow target host or downstream rate limit cannot consume every worker, connection or retry slot.
Delivery: assume at-least-once; ACK only after an idempotent stage effect is durable, and make redelivery safe.
Availability: scheduler failover may pause dispatch but cannot lose accepted jobs or duplicate an irreversible effect.
Operability: tenant identity must not become an unbounded metrics label; retain drill-down through sampled logs or a queryable fairness ledger.
capacity: Size the pipeline by peak submission rate with the daily volume beside it: ~25 rps peak (100k jobs/day) at T2, ~250 rps peak (1M jobs/day) at T3, ~25,000 rps peak (100M jobs/day) at T4. Tenant submission is steady B2B traffic, so plan 3–5× the average — except for a tenant running a bulk import, which concentrates like campaign traffic at 10–20×.

Judge the cost-aware scheduler per tier: not needed at T1, where one worker pool drains everything before anyone waits; worth it at T2, once a second tenant can delay the first; mandatory at T3, where one bulk import fills every worker for minutes; needs its own scaling story at T4, because the active-tenant set, the deficit state and the lease table stop fitting one scheduler process.
Model arrival rate, active tenants, jobs per burst, cost distribution and downstream limits separately; 10,000 registered users are not 10,000 simultaneously active queues.
Set each tenant's pending-cost cap from useful waiting time: admitted backlog must drain before its deadline at the tenant's guaranteed service rate.
Choose a fixed shard count from broker CPU, recovery time and hot-key skew, then benchmark it; hashing spreads load but does not provide fairness inside a shard.

Set consumer prefetch near measured executor concurrency and processing-time variance. Prefetch 1 is not a network round trip per message under steady push delivery, while a large value reserves invisible work at consumers.
Scale workers from oldest runnable age, admitted cost, service time and downstream headroom—not raw queue depth alone.
Reserve explicit capacity for interactive work and cap bulk share; shed bulk before borrowing capacity required by the interactive SLO.
en.diagram_title: Admission and cost-aware scheduling before RabbitMQ workers
data_model: Job — job_id, tenant_id, idempotency_key, stage, service_class, estimated_cost, deadline, attempt and state. The durable job store owns lifecycle; a broker delivery is a command to attempt one transition.
Tenant budget — tenant_id, tier, arrival rate, burst, pending_cost_limit, max_in_flight_cost and retry_budget. Version policy so an operator can explain why a job was admitted or rejected.

Scheduler state — active tenant, deficit, quantum, cursor and leased cost. Persist enough to rebuild safely; Redis may accelerate active-set operations but must not be the only record of accepted work.
Stage result — job_id, stage, input_version, output_reference and completed_at under a uniqueness constraint. The constraint turns redelivery into a no-op instead of a duplicate side effect.
Fairness event — decision id, tenant, policy version, charged cost, wait age and reason code. Keep it queryable with bounded retention rather than attaching tenant_id to every time-series metric.
stack: Admission API plus relational job store: commit accepted work and an outbox atomically, enforce idempotency and pending limits, and return 429 with Retry-After when the tenant budget is exhausted.

Deficit Round Robin dispatcher over active tenants: charge estimated work rather than message count, apply tier weights, lease jobs transactionally and publish through the outbox. Weighted Fair Queuing is an alternative when tighter latency bounds justify more scheduling cost.

RabbitMQ quorum queues for durable stage commands where replicated delivery is required; use a bounded set of queues by service class and shard, publisher confirms, manual ACKs and explicit dead-letter policy.

Separate channels/consumers with bounded executors: tune per-consumer prefetch to actual concurrency. RabbitMQ consumer priority selects preferred consumers; it is not tenant priority or a fairness algorithm.
Token buckets and bulkheads at downstream boundaries: enforce tenant/host/API concurrency after delivery because fair dispatch cannot prevent a long job from occupying every scarce connection.

Observability: publish scheduler lag, oldest runnable age by bounded tier, admitted/served cost share, in-flight cost, redelivery and DLQ age; provide sampled tenant drill-down outside high-cardinality metric labels.
tradeoffs: Queue per tenant vs bounded queues — dedicated queues give hard isolation and simple per-tenant visibility, but every queue replica is a broker process with metadata and recovery cost. Use them for a small active set or contractual isolation, not automatically for every registered account.

Hash shards vs fair scheduler — hashing is cheap and preserves tenant affinity, but collisions leave head-of-line blocking inside a shard. A scheduler adds state and a dispatch hop in exchange for an enforceable service share.

Message priority vs service classes — priority can move urgent ready messages ahead, but it does not measure tenant consumption and strict priority can starve lower classes. Prefer a few isolated queues with reserved worker shares when starvation is unacceptable.

Prefetch throughput vs fairness — larger prefetch amortizes delivery overhead and keeps workers busy, but reserves work outside broker visibility. Bound it by executor slots and variability instead of raising it until queue depth falls.

Exact cost vs estimated cost — message count is simple but unfair for heterogeneous jobs; perfect cost is unknowable before execution. Start with coarse weights, feed observed duration back into policy and cap estimation error with max in-flight cost.

Scheduler database vs Redis — a database makes accepted work and leases recoverable in one authority; Redis makes active-set scheduling fast. If Redis is used, rebuild it from durable job state and define behavior during cache loss.

Reserved interactive pool vs utilization — reservation protects latency during bulk floods but can idle. Allow controlled borrowing only when it is preemptible and the reserved capacity can be restored before the SLO is breached.

failure_review.question: What invariant can break?
failure_review.answer: An admitted tenant must make progress within its service contract, and a stage effect must occur at most once logically despite at-least-once delivery. Quotas, DRR deficit and idempotent stage records protect those two invariants.

failure_review.question: Which metric detects unfairness first?
failure_review.answer: Oldest runnable age and served-to-admitted cost share by bounded service tier reveal starvation before aggregate queue depth. Correlate them with scheduler lag, in-flight cost and downstream saturation.

failure_review.question: How is the blast radius contained?
failure_review.answer: Bound pending and in-flight cost per tenant, separate interactive from bulk capacity, and scope retry, connection and downstream limiters. A noisy tenant can exhaust only its own budget and shared bulk allowance.

failure_review.question: Can retry duplicate or reorder work?
failure_review.answer: Yes. ACK loss and consumer failure redeliver work, while delayed retries reorder it. Consumers fence state transitions by job/stage version, persist effects idempotently and guarantee ordering only for entities that require it.

failure_review.question: How do we repair and prove recovery?
failure_review.answer: Rebuild scheduler state from durable runnable and leased jobs, expire abandoned leases, replay the outbox with stable message IDs and reconcile stage results. Recovery is complete when old runnable age drains without duplicate effects or tier-share violations.

vi.title: Lập lịch work đa tenant công bằng với RabbitMQ
vi.excerpt: Ngăn 1.000 job của một tenant che mất job duy nhất của tenant khác bằng cách tách admission, scheduling và execution fairness, thay vì bắt prefetch giải cả ba.
vi.scope:
User gửi URL vào pipeline worker nhiều stage. Tenant A có thể enqueue 1.000 job trong khi tenant B gửi một job nhạy latency. Mục tiêu là thời gian chờ hữu hạn và resource share dự đoán được mà không tạo một queue cùng consumer cho mỗi tenant. RabbitMQ vẫn là durable delivery layer; scheduler hiểu cost mới sở hữu fairness.

Phân biệt cốt lõi: routing không phải scheduling. Hash tenant, tăng prefetch hay gán message priority có thể cải thiện distribution hoặc throughput, nhưng từng cách riêng lẻ không đảm bảo noisy tenant không độc chiếm downstream capacity.
functional: Nhận job kèm tenant id, idempotency key, service class, estimated cost và deadline; trả accepted, deferred hoặc rejected rõ ràng.
Áp per-tenant rate, pending-work và concurrent-cost limit trước khi publish runnable work.
Schedule active tenant bằng Deficit Round Robin, cho phép weight theo tier nhưng vẫn đảm bảo mọi tenant trong contract đều tiến triển.
Route job đã admit vào số lượng hữu hạn interactive/bulk queue, rồi giữ tenant context xuyên suốt mọi processing stage.
Retry lỗi transient bằng budget riêng và quarantine poison job mà không reset tenant cost.
Expose job state cùng cancellation mà không dùng vị trí trong RabbitMQ queue làm product source of truth.
quality: Fairness: bulk producer liên tục không thể khiến tenant đã admit chờ vô hạn; định nghĩa maximum runnable age cho mỗi service tier.
Backpressure: per-tenant và global backlog bị giới hạn theo số job lẫn estimated cost; overload trả 429 hoặc deferred trung thực trước khi broker memory thành giới hạn.
Isolation: retry, target host chậm hoặc downstream rate limit của một tenant không được ăn hết worker, connection hay retry slot.
Delivery: giả định at-least-once; chỉ ACK sau khi effect idempotent của stage đã durable và redelivery phải an toàn.
Availability: scheduler failover có thể tạm dừng dispatch nhưng không được làm mất accepted job hay lặp irreversible effect.
Operability: tenant identity không được thành metrics label vô hạn; drill-down qua sampled log hoặc fairness ledger có thể query.
capacity: Size pipeline theo peak submission rate, kèm daily volume trong ngoặc: ~25 rps peak (100k job/ngày) ở T2, ~250 rps peak (1 triệu job/ngày) ở T3, ~25.000 rps peak (100 triệu job/ngày) ở T4. Tenant submission là traffic B2B đều, nên tính 3–5× average — trừ tenant đang chạy bulk import, dồn như campaign traffic ở mức 10–20×.

Đánh giá cost-aware scheduler theo từng tier: không cần ở T1, khi một worker pool drain hết trước lúc có ai phải chờ; nên có ở T2, khi tenant thứ hai đã có thể làm tenant đầu chậm lại; bắt buộc ở T3, nơi một bulk import chiếm hết worker trong nhiều phút; cần scale riêng ở T4, vì active-tenant set, deficit state và lease table không còn vừa một scheduler process.
Model riêng arrival rate, active tenant, jobs mỗi burst, cost distribution và downstream limit; 10.000 registered user không đồng nghĩa 10.000 active queue cùng lúc.
Đặt pending-cost cap theo useful waiting time: admitted backlog phải drain trước deadline ở guaranteed service rate của tenant.
Chọn fixed shard count theo broker CPU, recovery time và hot-key skew rồi benchmark; hashing phân tán load nhưng không tạo fairness trong shard.

Đặt consumer prefetch gần executor concurrency và processing-time variance đã đo. Prefetch 1 không tạo một network round trip cho mỗi message trong steady push delivery, còn giá trị lớn giữ backlog vô hình ở consumer.
Scale worker theo oldest runnable age, admitted cost, service time và downstream headroom, không chỉ raw queue depth.
Reserve capacity rõ cho interactive work và cap bulk share; shed bulk trước khi mượn phần capacity cần để giữ interactive SLO.
vi.diagram_title: Admission và cost-aware scheduling trước RabbitMQ worker
data_model: Job — job_id, tenant_id, idempotency_key, stage, service_class, estimated_cost, deadline, attempt và state. Durable job store sở hữu lifecycle; broker delivery chỉ là lệnh thử một transition.
Tenant budget — tenant_id, tier, arrival rate, burst, pending_cost_limit, max_in_flight_cost và retry_budget. Version policy để operator giải thích được vì sao job được nhận hoặc từ chối.
Scheduler state — active tenant, deficit, quantum, cursor và leased cost. Persist đủ để rebuild an toàn; Redis có thể tăng tốc active-set nhưng không được là record duy nhất của accepted work.
Stage result — job_id, stage, input_version, output_reference và completed_at dưới unique constraint. Constraint biến redelivery thành no-op thay vì duplicate side effect.
Fairness event — decision id, tenant, policy version, charged cost, wait age và reason code. Giữ queryable với retention hữu hạn thay vì gắn tenant_id vào mọi time-series metric.
stack: Admission API cùng relational job store: commit accepted work và outbox atomically, enforce idempotency/pending limit, trả 429 kèm Retry-After khi tenant hết budget.

Deficit Round Robin dispatcher trên active tenant: tính estimated work thay vì message count, áp tier weight, lease job bằng transaction và publish qua outbox. Weighted Fair Queuing là lựa chọn khi latency bound chặt đáng trả scheduling cost cao hơn.
RabbitMQ quorum queue cho durable stage command khi cần replicated delivery; dùng tập queue hữu hạn theo service class và shard, publisher confirm, manual ACK cùng dead-letter policy rõ.

Channel/consumer riêng với bounded executor: tune per-consumer prefetch theo concurrency thật. RabbitMQ consumer priority chọn preferred consumer; nó không phải tenant priority hay fairness algorithm.
Token bucket và bulkhead tại downstream boundary: enforce tenant/host/API concurrency sau delivery vì fair dispatch không ngăn long job chiếm mọi scarce connection.

Observability: publish scheduler lag, oldest runnable age theo bounded tier, admitted/served cost share, in-flight cost, redelivery và DLQ age; tenant drill-down dùng sample ngoài metrics label high-cardinality.
tradeoffs: Queue per tenant vs bounded queues — dedicated queue cho hard isolation và visibility đơn giản, nhưng mỗi queue replica là một broker process kèm metadata/recovery cost. Chỉ dùng cho active set nhỏ hoặc isolation có hợp đồng, không tự động cho mọi account đăng ký.

Hash shard vs fair scheduler — hashing rẻ và giữ tenant affinity, nhưng collision vẫn gây head-of-line blocking trong shard. Scheduler thêm state và một dispatch hop để đổi lấy service share enforce được.

Message priority vs service class — priority có thể đưa urgent ready message lên trước, nhưng không đo tenant consumption và strict priority có thể làm đói class thấp. Dùng vài queue cô lập với reserved worker share khi không chấp nhận starvation.

Prefetch throughput vs fairness — prefetch lớn amortize delivery overhead và giữ worker bận nhưng reserve work ngoài broker visibility. Bound theo executor slot và variance thay vì tăng tới khi queue depth giảm.

Exact cost vs estimated cost — message count đơn giản nhưng bất công với job không đồng nhất; perfect cost không biết được trước execution. Khởi đầu bằng coarse weight, đưa observed duration về policy và cap estimation error bằng max in-flight cost.

Scheduler database vs Redis — database làm accepted work và lease recoverable trong một authority; Redis giúp active-set scheduling nhanh. Nếu dùng Redis, phải rebuild từ durable job state và định nghĩa behavior khi cache mất.

Reserved interactive pool vs utilization — reservation bảo vệ latency khi bulk flood nhưng có thể idle. Chỉ cho borrow có kiểm soát khi preemptible và restore được reserved capacity trước lúc breach SLO.

failure_review.question: Invariant nào có thể break?
failure_review.answer: Tenant đã admit phải tiến triển trong service contract, và stage effect chỉ được xảy ra một lần về mặt logic dù delivery at-least-once. Quota, DRR deficit cùng idempotent stage record bảo vệ hai invariant này.

failure_review.question: Metric nào phát hiện unfairness đầu tiên?
failure_review.answer: Oldest runnable age và served/admitted cost share theo bounded service tier lộ starvation trước aggregate queue depth. Correlate với scheduler lag, in-flight cost và downstream saturation.

failure_review.question: Blast radius được contain thế nào?
failure_review.answer: Bound pending/in-flight cost theo tenant, tách interactive khỏi bulk capacity, scope retry, connection và downstream limiter. Noisy tenant chỉ làm cạn budget riêng cùng shared bulk allowance.

failure_review.question: Retry có duplicate hoặc reorder work không?
failure_review.answer: Có. ACK loss và consumer failure gây redelivery, delayed retry làm reorder. Consumer fence state transition theo job/stage version, persist effect idempotently và chỉ guarantee order cho entity thực sự cần.

failure_review.question: Repair và prove recovery thế nào?
failure_review.answer: Rebuild scheduler state từ durable runnable/leased job, expire lease bị bỏ, replay outbox bằng stable message ID và reconcile stage result. Recovery xong khi old runnable age drain mà không có duplicate effect hay vi phạm tier share.
